name: Chambal Fertilisers & Chemicals Ltd
title: Chambal Fertilisers & Chemicals Ltd - 500085 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA up 56% to Rs 255 crore on urea mix and ammonia, but receivables jumped to Rs 2,075 crore and TAN capacity ramp (240,000 tpa) is the main new supply-side driver.

capex.quote: The total put together should be around Rs. 500 crores balance, I mean, Urea and TAN put together.

triggers.label: TAN 240,000 tpa enters commissioning
triggers.quote: has a capacity of 240,000 metric tons per annum, representing Chambal's strategic entry into industrial and mining chemicals

triggers.label: Receivables Rs 367 cr → Rs 2,075 cr
triggers.quote: total receivables stood at about Rs. 2,075 crores, comprising market debt of Rs. 121 crores and subsidy receivables of Rs. 1,954 crores

triggers.label: Ammonia pricing lifts Q4 urea margin
triggers.quote: We do know that we do sell a certain amount of Ammonia, so we had better margins there.

triggers.label: Fourth urea plant planning advanced
triggers.quote: as far as the fourth plant in terms of Urea is concerned, we are at very, very advanced in terms of execution of this

guidance.quote: we have roughly about 1,60,000 - 1,70,000 tons of production would be possible
the normal routine Capex of the order of about Rs. 170-180 crores
we will definitely exceed what we did this year

red_flags.label: Receivables jump to Rs 2,075 cr with short-term borrowing rising
red_flags.quote: total receivables stood at about Rs. 2,075 crores, comprising market debt of Rs. 121 crores and subsidy receivables of Rs. 1,954 crores

red_flags.label: Complex fertiliser EBIT margin ~4% in FY26
red_flags.quote: EBIT margins stood at around 4 % during FY '26

red_flags.label: Gas cost USD 18+ and industry margin pressure
red_flags.quote: industry margins would remain under pressure due to high raw material costs and rupee depreciation

evasions.topic: Ammonia volume and EBITDA per ton split
evasions.quote: Okay, that you discuss offline with Mr. Anuj Jain.
Too premature to give you any guidance on this, but it is moving.
